articleTitle: Modulator and Form of Modulation Suitable for Digital Communication Achieving Low Far-Out Side-Bands Levels Without the use of Filters: Proposed as a Modification to the Global Satellite Navigation System Glonass
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A form of Continuous Phase Modulation is proposed as a modification to standard QPSK. The amptitude of the modulated carrier is identically constant but the phase makes half-cycle cosinusoidal transitions between its four discrete states. The power spectrum falls as (frequency from carrier)<sup>-6</sup>. A “proofoPconcept” modulator has been built in hardware at 16 MHz which is approximately 1/100th of the GLONASS carrier frequency. This confirms the expected form of the power spectrum. There appears to be no reason why it should not be scaled up to the GLONASS frequency. If adopted by GLONASS it would ameliorate the EMC problem existing between GLONASS and the Radio Astronomy Service.

articleTitle: Exploration of Turbulent Atmosphere Features by Using Radiorefractometers with Spatial Diversity
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper the possibility to reconstruct phase fluctuations of electromagnetic wave propagating in turbulent atmosphere upon registration of its log-amplitude is shown. By means of this recovery electromagnetic compatibility of radiochannels in complex interference environment may be substantially enhanced. Experimental results of same important characteristics of random medium model determination are presented.

articleTitle: EMC in CB Radio
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: CB radio has been known for many years and is still very popular. A lot of users everyday meet problems with EMC in the system. CB users are everywhere and they have to keep an eye on interference in TV, radio broadcast and in acoustic amplifiers caused by their radios. The authors of this article, users of CBs for some years now analysed many of the common EMC troubles and described some of them.

articleTitle: The Conversion Factors for Radio Interference from Electrified Railway Measured with Different Detectors
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Based on 1400 measured APD’s on three railway lines, the paper analyses V<inf>qp</inf>, V<inf>rms</inf>, V<inf>ave</inf> calculated by cook’s method and presents the conversion factors 11.3 dB and 17.8dBfor V<inf>qp</inf>/V<inf>rms</inf> and V<inf>qp</inf>/V<inf>ave</inf>. The factors are applicable to CISPR 6-dB bandwidth of 9KHz.

articleTitle: Method of Convolution Difference for Calculating Electromagnetic Compatibility Indexes by Periodical Disturbances
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The filter reaction calculation method of dynamic models of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) indexes has been developed. The phenomenon of quasi-weigt function has been introduced. For unification of calculation the filter is represented by aperiodical links. For fragment-linear disturbances the solution has been obtained in final form. The efficiency of the method has been illustrated on the example of electromagnetic compatibility evaluation by oscillations dose and flicker sharpness level for fourth-order differential equation. The EMC conditions have been determined when rolling mills operating. The conclusion has been drawn as for incorrectness of voltage fluctuation evaluation by fluctuation changes and frequencies.

articleTitle: Spurious Radiation of Rectenna Receiving-Rectifying Elements
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The characteristics of the rectennas spurious radiation - the total radiation power and their radiation pattern on the highest harmonics frequencies are considered. The offered methods of the rectennas analysis is based on the general method of antennas with nonlinear elements analysis developed by the authors. The plots, illustrating the change of the spurious radiation level and structure of various variants of the rectennas single receiving-rectifying elements (RRE), depending on the power value incident on the RRE, the type of radiators used in them, the RRE circuit, are given.

articleTitle: Application of the EMC Directive in the Field of Electrodomestic Appliances
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Manufacturers of household appliances are well aware of the changing e.m. environments for their products, the increasing consumer demands on performance and reliability, as well as the developments in standardization and legislation. The Generic Immunity Standard EN 50082-1, 1992, made mandatory within the European Community by means of the EMC Directive 89/336/EEC, is too coarse for the variety of household appliances. The immunity requirements are too severe for some appliances but too relaxed for many others, leading to overtesting and to complaints in the market. In a combined action of the CENELEC Technical Committees 61 and 110A a new draft immunity standard was formulated, prEN 55014-2, discussed in the IEC as draft CISPR 14-2. The presentation deals with the development of the standard, and with the proposed immunity requirements for the four categories of household appliances in comparison to those of the generic immunity standard. The differences will be elucidated.

articleTitle: Review and Future Research of Gtem Cells
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: History and present research and developments (1984-93), incl. modifications of the old GTEM cell, is reviewed. The two important patents are highlighted, including still existing imperfections in the design, mainly assigned to the broad band termination. Considering even the latest research in Europe, US and Far East there are still unsolved problems in fully understanding all parameters, that might improve the field quality for immunity testing and emissions modeling. Marketing statements of license manufacturers "The GTEM is OK up to 18 GHz" are lacking final scientific prove. The amended list of potentially new and required GTEM research details identified target areas. The authors are skeptical about meaningful expansions of the GTEM concept to gigantic (16m long, 3.5 m septum height) cells, before truly solving existing imperfections. We are consequently restricting ourselves to fundamental, theoretical and experimental research efforts for practical EMI investigations, bearing economy in mind.

articleTitle: Ground Noise Characterization by its Equivalent Thevenin Generator
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of the common mode emission produced by ground noise on a PCB is theoretically and experimentally investigated. In particular, considering a cable connected to the ground plane, the source of cable common mode current is modelled by a Thevenin representation: the knowledge of the ground plane current distribution allows to define the equivalent Thevenin generator and its internal impedance, both strongly dependent on frequency and cable connection point.

articleTitle: An Overview of the New Radiocommunication Sector of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) with Emphasis on the Science Services Study Group
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The ITU Radiocommunications (ITU-R) Sector is organized such that the Members can exchange technical views and develop recommendations on the use of the radio spectrum for a variety of critical radio services. Among these services are a group of very special radio based activities known collectively as the Science Services. These radio services are the Space Research Service, the Earth Exploration Satellite Service, the Meteorological Satellite Service, the Radio and Radar Astronomy Service, and the Time and Frequency Standard Service. Study Group 7 of the ITU-R is responsible for dealing with these services and, since 1970, has been developing the radio spectrum utilization criteria for the extremely complex and sensitive techniques employed by the services. These techniques are applied in both terrestrial and space-borne environments and have opened the door to a great many scientific achievements giving mankind a much greater understanding of our environment and how it affects our lives. Each presentation in today's Symposium session will highlight one or more of these services and illustrate many of the important discoveries evolving from them.

articleTitle: The ESF Committee on Radio Astronomy Frequencies
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio astronomy is a passive service. It cannot cause interference to any other service. However, it suffers increasingly fron man-made interference so that in some frequency bands allocated to radio astronomy observations can sometimes not be done at all. This is partly due to the techniques used in radio astronomy, i.e. the signal detected lies usually about 60 dB below system noise.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Lightning Protection Systems
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper reports on an effort to develop a computationally efficient technique for simulating the interaction of direct-strike lightning with the lightning protection installations. The technique is based upon the frequency-domain electric field integral equation formulation combined with the method of moments, and incorporates all the wave phenomena associated with the installation. The primary intended application of the method is the prediction of direct effects on the lightning protection system (LPS) of a building, and thus the optimization of the LPS design. Numerical examples illustrating the potentiality of the method are given. Theoretical predictions are compared with experimental data obtained from laboratory model measurements.

articleTitle: Update on EMC Regulations in Germany and Europe Respectively
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The status of cited regulations and referenced standards is Dec. 1993. This paper is an extension with many new pieces of EC EMC information and amendments over a tutorial given at the IEEE EMC Symposium Japan 94. Based on the European EMC directive 89/336/EEC and its amended extension of the transitional period up to 1. of Jan. 1996 the German EMC law has been brought into force on 13. of Nov. 1992. In spite the fact of old national regulations and procedures, still in existence, during the transitional period, parallel interim procedures have been issued recently in order to match and harmonize German to European EMC Standards and Regulations. The peculiarity is the sometimes generated confusion by the different legal requirements in the various national EU member countries. Inherent imperfections in transposing the directive into national law become evident by analyzing the legal consequences for committed violations. Germany defines this as a fine of up to 100000 DEM, while the UK considers this a criminal act with possibly three month of imprisonment. It is consequently important to learn about the precise interim requirements for EMC certification of products to be imported e.g. into Germany one of the biggest markets within the European Union. This scenario will be elucidated by a number of tables, following case studies, incl. recommended solutions. These are based on the first author's experience as a EMC testhouse assessor for the accreditation system in Germany and EES's permanent involvement into this process as an active testhouse. Finally a summary will be given on the legal status of the implementation of the transposition of the EC EMC directive in the various EC member countries. Additionally a full list of all relevant German postal decrees will be presented for the first time in a symposium publication.

articleTitle: High Voltage Electrostatic Fields Effect for Biological Safety of Computer Operators and its Protection
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Already 30 years have passed when the cathoderay tubes was occupied the main position of display equipment for computer on behalf of the card leader and holing tape systems. During 30 years, many biological effects were discovered in this term, such as; (1) fall of eyesight of VDT operators (2) The suspicion of face skin cancer of VDT operators by the strong electrostatic charge of CRT tube. (3) Biological effects against the woman health by the ELF and VLF magnetic fields which generated by CRT and CPU equipments, and (4) Psycchological problems of VDT operators by the effect of closed working environment. In this paper, we explain our improvement result for strong electrostatic field reduction at the front of CRT tube, and explain about activities of new committee for protection of above problems.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of the Earth Currents in a Ground Wire System Under the Condition of Thunderstorm -New Method for the Discrimination of Electro-Static and Magnetic Noise Due to Lightning-
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For the purpose of analyzing the induced voltage on aerial lines caused by lightning, the preliminary study of measuring the earth current in a simplified ground wire system have been carried out under the condition of far lightning in sumer. Possibilities of producing electro-magnetic induced noises or damages on power-distribution and communication line systems are discussed. New idea to decrease an electro-magnetic induction effect and to discriminate the induced voltages of rotational and non-rotational field are presented.

articleTitle: Satellite Earth Stations with Small Antenna (VSAT) as a Source of Interference
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The article presents analysis of satellite earth station with small antenna, VSAT, as a source of interference. For that purpose, basic paths of interference emission from the station and interference frequency characteristics have been determined. Next, the parameters which are essential from a compatibility analysis point of view and necessary for creating a mathematical model of the station have been defined. For that purpose, information contained in European standards of ETSI which describe the VSAT satellite station have been utilized. Based on the model, appropriate analyses were conducted which enabled determination of interference threat degree. Moreover, a method of frequency coordination enabling softening of licence assignment procedure is presented.

articleTitle: On Using a Reverberation Chamber for HPM Interaction Studies
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the reverberation chamber concept is analyzed for application to HPM interaction studies. A theoretical study is performed for a simple wire configuration and for a general receiving antenna. Illumination by a microwave beam oriented and polarized for maximum excitation is considered along with illumination provided by an ideal mode- stirred reverberation chamber that simulates plane-wave illumination varying over all possible directions of incidence and all possible polarizations. An evaluation of the use of a reverberation chamber to perform HPM studies is presented including the limitations, advantages, and disadvantages.

articleTitle: Field Distribution Inside of an Open Tem Transmission Line
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Operation of TEM lines for radiated susceptibility (RS) testing inside a shielded enclosure can cause large errors because of room resonances. The repercussions of these resonances upon the field uniformity inside the strip line are investigated. The quality of automatic field strength control at a reference point inside the line and the field uniformity are checked for various arrangements of small ferrite and pyramid absorbers close to the waveguide structure. Satisfactory performance is obtained with a simple solution at low cost.

articleTitle: The Radio Universe
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Over 100 years ago a great pioneer of ionospheric research, A.E. Kennelly, proposed to Edison that they should collaborate in detecting radio waves from the Sun. He wrote to Lick Observatory as follows: Along with the electromagnetic disturbances we receive from the Sun which of course we recognise as light and heat, it is not unreasonable to suppose that there will be disturbances of much longer wavelength. If so, we might translate them into sound.

articleTitle: The Peculiarities of High-Frequency EMP Simulation Under Resonance Interaction with the Screen-Casings of an Object
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The present-day problem in the light of IEC recommendations on the EMC is the development of new techniques for experimental estimation of stability of radio electronic apparatus. These techniques would provide for the highest authenticity of simulation. The perspective technique for the stability tests of apparatus located inside the screen-casings which are influenced by high-frequency EMP (HF EMP) has been developed taking into account the fact that the interaction of noise-carrying field with the object has resonance character.

articleTitle: Investigation of a System of Nonlinear Interference Sources
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The scattering characteristics of a system of nonlinear interference sources are investigated. Dependencies of the scattered field on the distance between separate nonlinear interference sources, the location of nonlinear insertion in them, the angular distribution of the scattered field at the double frequency have been defined theoretically and checked experimentally. Experimental and theoretical results are in a good quantitative and qualitative agreement. This model of the nonlinear contact interference sources allows one to calculate the intensity of the interferences with taking into account their mutual influence and may be useful for the solution of EMC problems.

articleTitle: Discrimination of Weakly-Directed Antennas with a Comb of Small Size
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Practical possibility of discrimination of weakly- directed antennas with a finite distance each from other on a metal screen by means of several resonance grooves of the structure with lateral dimensions being equal 0.5 1.5 of wavelength was investigated. By experimental results empirical formulas and nomograms for determination of parameters of discriminating comb by the given frequency range, the required value of discrimination and the distance the antennas from the location of discrimination structure were obtained. The results could be used for solving the problem of provision of inter system EMC RES.

articleTitle: Earth Exploration Satellite (EES) Service and Meteorological Satellite (METSAT) Service
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EES and METSAT radiocommunication services include a number of systems for scientific and/ or application purposes. Such systems perform a variety of functions, some of them using transmission links between earth stations and satellites, and others using sensing links for both passive and active microwave remote sensing. Interference criteria must be determined in order to allow sharing of frequencies with other spectrum users. Major progress is currently being made in refining interference criteria so as to facilitate sharing, while permitting EES system designers to retain effective control over EES system performance.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Possibility of the Near-Field Concentration and Steering within the Human Tissue-Equivalent Phantoms
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Under investigation is the problem of the near-field concentration and steering within the human tissue-equivalent phantoms, excitated by the phased annular array. The problem of the array excitation synthesis was considered and the field distribution analysis within the cylindrical phantoms was carried out. The condition of the maximum field concentration in the tissue-equivalent lossy dielectrical bodies were determined and the possibility of steering the near-field distribution maximum within the object being excitated was investigated. The condition of minimum irradiation to the outer space under the phantom excitation was determined.

articleTitle: An Approach of Rule Development for Reflection and Crosstalk Effects on Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the design and the development of rules for a fast calculation of reflection and crosstalk effects on printed circuit boards. The rules are applied to the preanalysis of complex PCB. In the first part of this paper, the reflection behaviour of two-point-nets with ohmic terminations is described. The introduced rule base enables a preanalysis with respect to the voltage overshoot at the receiver. Furthermore, the dependence of the voltage overshoot from the length of the transmission line is investigated. The reflection behaviour of three-point-nets is analyzed with respect to their geometrical structure. The examination of crosstalk effects is described in the second part of this paper. Based on a heuristic approach, an improved formula for crosstalk estimation is presented. Currently, the calculations are valid for a structure of two coupled transmission lines.

articleTitle: Non-Loading Inductive Couplers for Driving Cables
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In designing EMP simulators for various systems to be tested, one is often faced with the case of long conductors (cables) to be illuminated. In some cases this can be accomplished by local pulsers which are inductively coupled to the cable. This paper considers the design of such devices with particular attention to the requirement of small equivalent source impedance (compared to the cable (antenna) impedance) so as to not significantly change the complex resonance frequencies. Various other aspects, such as the exciting waveform and distribution of multiple inductive drivers, are also considered.

articleTitle: EMC of Power Radars and Television Receivers
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This work reports on the results of researches of influence of amission of power impulse radars on television receivers. Practical recommendations for secure of EMC of impulse radars and TV receivers are adduced in conclusion.

articleTitle: An Elf Signal to Noise Model for Radio Propagation in Shallow Sea Water
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We consider a signal to noise model relating to propagation in sub-surface regions where the radiation source is a buried electric or magnetic dipole and the effects of atmospheric noise penetrating into the sub-surface layer are required. We concentrate upon the air-sea-seabed case and numerical evaluation of relevant Sommerfeld integrals has enabled the fields in the sea produced by submerged sources to be estimated. Measurements of the natural Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) radio noise (known as Schumann resonances) in the period 1988 to 1989 have enabled average atmospheric noise levels and Schumann resonance parameters to be deduced. At 45 Hz the average measured electric field was 41.6 dBµV/m<tex>$\sqrt{\text{H}_{\text{Z}}}$</tex>. The noise fields can be estimated at any giyen depth below the ground (or sea) surface from the measured values in the air. We present results showing the computed fields produced in the sea from a submerged horizontal electric dipole man-made source and compare this with the sub-surface atmospheric noise fields deduced from the experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Direction Finding of Whistlers and Their Causative Atmospherics Observed at One Station
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The simultaneous location of the ionospheric exit region of whistlers and of their causative atmospherics is known to be very important in the extensive study of the propagation mechanism of whistlers along the total path from the source to the receiver. The direction finding to locate the ionospheric exit region of whistlers has been currently used in investigating the propagation characteristics of whistlers, whistler ducts, and magnetospheric plasma dynamics<sup>[2]-[5]</sup>. But the simultaneous location of the ionospheric exit regions of whistlers and their causative atmospherics has so far been lacking without very few trial<sup>[6], [7]</sup>, which would be of great importance in the study of whistlers. There are two kind of direction finding methods for causative atmospherics of whistler. One is to know the direction<sup>[2],[65]</sup> using the goniometer, and another is to know the distance using the curve fitting method of the tweek<sup>[7]-[8]</sup>, which is the waves propagated from the source to the receiver. But these methods require multi-stations separated more over 1000km to locate the causative atmospheric. And even if having these multi-stations, we can not locate the point on the special case shown in Fig. 1. So, we have developed the so- called "field analysis method" direction finding system to locate the ionospheric exit point of whistler and ionospheric reflective point of tweek for measuring the direction at one station based on the simultaneous measurement of two horizontal magnetic field components and one vertical electric field component[4]-[6], [9]. And the distance from the causative atmospheric to the observation point is measured using the curve fitting method of tweek.

articleTitle: EMP - Vulnerability Tests for Electronic Devices and Systems
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a direct and indirect method of electromagnetic compatibility testing. The tests were run at the Electromagnetic Compatibility Laboratory (EMCL), Institute of Telecommunication and Acoustics, Technical University of Wrocław, Poland.

articleTitle: Influence of Nonlinear Loads on the Transient Response of a Field-Excited Network
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A general procedure for the analysis of a field-excited network containing multiconductor lossy lines with any load condition is presented. The nonlinear loads are replaced by unknown current sources. The open-ended and short-circuited branches of the network are simulated by the connection of parallel matrix conductances G and -G, and series matrix resistances R and -R, respectively. The transient voltages and currents at each port of the network are computed by solving numerically the Volterra matrix equations obtained by applying the nodal approach in the time-domain. The boundary conditions include the functions describing the nonlinear elements behaviour and additional expressions concerning the presence of the negative matrices -G and -R. Constraints on the load characteristics are defined to obtain a unique solution for the equation system. The analysis of the convergence and stability properties of the procedure is carried out, in order to evaluate the influence of the different load conditions. The EMP-induced effects on a signal mesh-type network with nonlinear loads, open-ended and short-circuited branches are computed.

articleTitle: Study Group 7 Space Research (Working Party 7B) Activities
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper addresses the telecommunications requirements of the space research service, involving both near-Earth and deep-space missions. These two kinds of activity cannot easily share frequencies and separate criteria have been developed for their protection and sharing with other services. The relevant Recommendations and associated texts of the ITU-R are reviewed The most recent work in deriving these Recommendations has been conducted within Working Party 7B of Study Group 7. The Space Frequency Coordination Group (SFCG), administered via a secretariat in the European Space Agency, does much useful work in establishing global procedures to avoid interference between systems operating in the space services bands.

articleTitle: Hypophyseal and Adrenocortical Changes in Rats Exposed Repeatedly in E Field of 227 kHz
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: After exposure of adult male and female rats 2 hrs daily for 44 or 46 consecutive days to E field of 227 kHz at 200 V/m the weight of anterior pituitary thyroid, adrenal, and gonadal glands was lower by 16.4%, 11.4%, 13%, 19.0% and 19.7 % and 32.4 %, respectively, in comparison to such glands in control animals. The anterior pituitary gland contained 13.0% less LH in exposed male rats and 35 % less LH in exposed female rats, and 40 % less GH in exposed female rats than in control animals. There was no changes of these descriptors in rats exposed 5 hrs daily for 67 consecutive days to E field of 227 kHz at 50 V/m.

articleTitle: The Receiving Antenna Height Gain in the Process of Frequency Planning
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The conference in frame of the preparation of the final version of the international agreement Vienna Agreement' 93 [1] raised several technical problems, which have not been unambiguously defined and worked out, until now. One of these problems is the calculation and the practical application of the receiving antenna height gain f<inf>h</inf> (RAHG).

articleTitle: Improvement of Microwave Oven Leak-Proofness
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One quarter wavelength choke properties have been revised for the microwave oven door choke seal and optimum dimensions emerged. Power leakage from the 2.45 GHz, 800 W domestic microwave oven with improved door choke seal has been decreased to the minimum level, that is determined by radiation throught the oven screen holes. Simultaneously, decreasing of radiation in the TV satellit frequency band has been observed.

articleTitle: Noise, Fluctuations, Chaos, and EMC
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since the advent of a new concept of ’chaos', its study has developed rapidly in recent years in various fields of science. ‘Chaos’ is a most remarkable feature as well as a ubiquitous mode of appearance in nature, and is considered to be most basic, practical, and important, without an exception, for EMC problems, since chaos is thought to be a source-origin of electromagnetic interference, particularly when it is severe. In this paper, some of recent topics on ‘Noise, Fluctuations, and Chaos’ are reviewed briefly from EMC aspects, based on papers at a series of Wroclaw Symposia and Tokyo Workshops and Symposia.

articleTitle: Time Domain Near Field Antenna Measurements
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The peculiarities of time domain near zone direct measurement technique with ultrashort sounding signal are described. The time domain method of the antenna pattern restoration from measurement data is compared with the frequency domain one. Radiation pulse field space-time variations of aperture antennas are analyzed.

articleTitle: Interference Due to Rain Scatter Involving a Feeder Link and an Urban Radio Relay System
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An arrangement constituted by a satellite feeder link sited in an urban area and a locai network of radio links operating in the same frequency band (18 GHz) has been simulated over a large amount of vertical (RHI) radar scans in order to estimate the concurrent effects of rain scatter coupling and attenuation along the interferred path, both contributing to the degradation of the radio system performance.

articleTitle: Transfer Impedance of Overlapping Braided Cable Shields and Hose Clamp Shield Terminations
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Surface transfer impedance measurements of overlapping cable braids on a large cable showed that the transfer impedance of this joining technique was not a sensitive function of the amount of overlap or the technique for applying pressure to the braids. Measurements of the transfer impedance of a hose clamp braid termination that increased the braid diameter by a almost a factor of three showed that the low frequency transfer impedance of the braid termination was about 1/6 of the low frequency transfer impedance of a meter of cable. The high frequency transfer impedance of the hose clamp braid termination was about 1/12 that of a meter of cable.

articleTitle: Modeling Problems of Pulse Processes in the Transmission Lines with the Equivalent Circuits
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is shown that the process of electromagnetic wave propagation in the transmission line described by telegrapher equations and the process in the equivalent circuit don't coincide. In the case of process reproduction is too big, and it does not subside with the increase of the number of the equivalent circuit sections. To eliminate this phenomenon two approaches are suggested. The first one is based on working out special difference scheme stencils for finite-difference approximation of telegrapher equations. The second one is based on solving the task of approximation of the characteristics in the frequency or time domain of the line with the help of equivalent circuits. Numerical examples are given.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Currents Induced in the Organs of a Human Body by a Vertical 60 Hz, 10 kV/m Electric Field
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We have developed a numerical method to predict the currents induced in the organs of a human body by an ELF-LF electric field. We describe the method and present, for a 60 Hz, 10 kV/m field, predicted values for five different body heights, two different postures and body-ground impedances ranging from 0 to 1 Gigaohms.

articleTitle: New Theory of Source Mechanism for Seismogenic Electromagnetic Emissions Based on the Recent Results of Statistic Analysis
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The study of electromagnetic emission phenomena related to earthquakes was started since 1980 as the cooperative project between Japan and U.S.S.R. The first emissions were observed at 16:33 JST (UT + 9hours) on March 31, 1980, at Sugadaira Space Radio Observatory, University of Electro-Communications, Sugadaira, Nagano Japan. Observation frequency was 81kHz and the magnitude of this earthquake was about 7. The depth of focus was approximately 380 km and the location of epicenter was in the Kyoto prefecture and the distance between epicenter and Sugadaira Observatory was approximately 250 km. The record of receiver output shows an anomalously high change in the back ground noise level of 81 kHz more than 15dB over the usual level, beginning 50 minuts before the main shock. At same time, the VLF wide-band whistler recorder at Sugadaira Observatory also registered unusual impulsive emissions at frequencies below 1.5 kHz before the earthquake (Gokhberg et.al.1982).

articleTitle: ETSI - The European Telecommunications Standards Institute
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Looking at the present political situation in Europe, we are witnessing a very exciting period: • The European Community is becoming reality. • After a period of forty years of the Cold War between East and West, the countries in Central and Eastern Europe are discovering their national identity. In order to achieve this objective, a lot of hard work, initiative, creativity, cleverness, money and patience have to be invested... In this context, proper working of telecommunications will play a role of utmost importance.

articleTitle: Industrial Pipe-Lines as Elements of Complex Grounding System
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Industrial pipe-lines are natural elements of a common complex grounding system at modem industrial enterprise. This paper suggests a solution of problems, concerning integrated reliable and safe operation of electrical installations and service lines. The new method offers higher efficiency of grounding system's protective functions and allows to avoid installation of additional and expensive artificial grounding connections.

articleTitle: Quantifying the Accuracy of Numerical Modelung Tools for EMC Problems
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to gain confidence in the use of numerical modelling tools they need to be validated against experimental results. No absolute method exists to enable a simple quantitative evaluation of the accuracy of these tools, where performance over a range of frequencies is required. This paper will present a technique, based on correlation functions, which provides a simple method for objective comparisons between simulated and experimental results and between different sets of simulated results.

articleTitle: Low-Pass Filter-Limiter Based on a High-Temperature Superconductor, Protecting Radioelectronics Equipment from EMI up to 10 GHz
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New superconducting low pass filter-limiter containing two switching high- T<inf>c</inf> elements is presented. Its operating principle is based on the fast film switching from superconducting (S) state to the normal conducting (N) state under controlling overcriticall current pulses or under input parasitic pulses. The phenomenon of the fast (≤ 10<sup>-10</sup> s) S-N switching in the superconductive films under an electromagnetic impulse (EMI) is considered as well.

articleTitle: Simulation of Influences on General Multiconductor Transmission Line Structures
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: If high-frequency interfering signals are propagating on electrically long transmission paths, attention must be paid to both transmission line interference and radiation coupling to guarantee the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). The interference voltages and currents on the transmission line system, which are coupled by distributed capacities and inductivities, depend on the line parameters, the elements of termination, the length of line and the occurring signals. The calculation of trouble signals on the line system as a function of path and time can usually be performed only numerically. This paper deals with a numerical computing method, which allows non-uniform, time-variant and nonlinear proportions.

articleTitle: The Glonass-Radio Astronomy Joint Experiment
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The global satellite navigation system GLONASS has caused immense harm to radio astronomical measurements of the hydroxyl radical in the band 1610.6-1613.8 MHz. Discussions between IUCAF and the GLONASS administration led to a joint experiment in November 1992 which tested various proposals to reduce the harmful interference. Results of the experiment indicate that the impact of GLONASS on radio astronomy can be considerably reduced by reconfiguring the frequencies of the satellite constellation within the existing channels. However further means will need to be found to reduce the interference below the harmful thresholds specified in ITU-R Recommendation 769.

articleTitle: Absorption Characteristics of Lossy Finite-Length Cylindrical Human Model
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Health hazards of electromagnetic radiation are determined by the electrical properties of tissues, frequency and distance. In this study, man is modeled by multi-layer cylindrical dielectric layers to predict the absorption characteristics of different part of man (i.e. skin, fat, cloth, etc.) in several different sized. The simulation results of this model have been compared to the multilayered infinite-size cylinder and planer models by using realistic parameters encountered in the field of dosimetry. The results are also compared and discussed with experimental and published results available in the literature. A good consistency are obtained.

articleTitle: Cenelec and its EMC Programme
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: THIS YEAR'S symposium has come at an opportune time, since CENELEC, the European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardization, is in the process of unveiling a whole range of new standards, generic and product family standards, which, when successfully implemented in at least 18 European countries, will make a major contribution to the harmonious nature of our increasingly diverse electrical environment. But first, what exactly is CENELEC? Why is it there?

articleTitle: A Review of Tem Cell Development
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper will review work done on the development and use of TEM cells for EMC related measurements. Topics considered are; characteristic impedance, TEM mode field distribution, higher-order modes, cell resonances, test object loading, source emissions, broadband TEM cells and hybrid TEM cell reverberation chambers. The purpose of the paper is to review the literature, summarize previous analytical work, characterize the present state of TEM cell research, and discuss problems requiring further investigation.

articleTitle: A Analysis of Generation and Radiation of Crossmodulation Harmonics
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new analytical method for the solving of the nonlinear scattering problems based on the application on nonlinear boundary conditions was given in earliar paper is applied for new EMC problems solution. A number of model problems, which permit to come to new conclusions about the influence of cylindrical bodies with a few transversal gaps for the case of beharmonic excitation and cross joints in waveguide lines on EMC, are considered.

articleTitle: Calculation of Conductive Effects on System of Two Coupled Underground Conductors
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a method of the solution for the potentials excited along conductively and inductively coupled conductors by conductive effects of complex earthing arrangements. It is assumed that the system considered is linear and that the earth is an isotropic, homogeneous medium of finite conductivity. The reaction of currents flowing in the underground conductors on the potential excited in the earth by the earthing devices (primary potential) is disregarded. The transmission line model of the conductor with earth return, a segmental approximation of the curve of the primary potential distribution along the conductor and the concept of superposition have been used in the method. The method may be useful for evaluation of conductive effects on underground conductors in many practical cases, which are connected with power supply systems, electric traction and cathodic protection as well. The technical application of the method presented is illustrated by an example.

articleTitle: Standardization in the EMC Field - South African Perspective
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents process and current status of standardization in the EMC field in the context of an African country. It covers legal developments, regulatory and policing aspects as well as adaptation of international and development of local standards in the EMC field. Specific EMC environment of the third/first world country is also discussed.

articleTitle: Ecological Monitoring of Electromagnetic Fields of a Large City
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic fields created by radio equipment have a disastrous influence on man's health. In Kazan University ecological monitoring system of of electromagnetic field (EMF) has been created. That make it possible to check EMF by theoretically-calculated and measuring methods. Electromagnetic field intensity calculated agree well with control measurements for ultra short waves range (30-1000 Miz). On the basis the computer map of electromagnetic fields has been created for Kazan. For daily control of electromagnetic field level in the range 3-30 Miz automatic measuring complex "Cyclon" has been made.

articleTitle: Survey of Lightning and Lemp Sessions
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The papers in the two “Lightning and LEMP” sessions cover a large spectrum of subjects from lightning phenomenology to protection concepts.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment for the Protection Against Lemp of Structures with Electronic Equipment
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the assessment of lightning hazard for the structures containing electronic equipment with connections to surroundings. Effects of electromagnetic interaction of direct as well as remote strokes have been taken into account by means of critical dimensions of lightning collection areas, probabilities of partial damages and relevant weighting coefficients. A composition of partial probabilities and weighting coefficients has been developed and used as factor indicating the need and efficiency of protection.

articleTitle: Influence of Panel Patterns on VHF and UHF Antenna Systems Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In design process, ERP of transmitting station (which is a base of international coordinations), is evaluated from calculated antenna system HRP and VRP. If antenna system design is not enough precise, then probability of interferences in relations to other services is growing. In paper influence of the antenna panel phase radiation pattern (RP) for antenna system resulting RP are discussed. On practical antenna systems examples, RPs obtained exactly and without taken into consideration panel phase RP are compared. Presented results showed, that panel phase RP has substantial influence for the most important antenna system parameters: horizontal RP and vertical RP (HRP and VRP).

articleTitle: Abnormal Electromagnetic Signals Appeared in Osaka (Japan)
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mysterious electric phenomena appeared in a new embroidery factory, which was in the City of Higashi(East)-Osaka, for more than one year from October 1990. Fires, which were caused by the unknown current, broke out five times in the factory. Many curious phenomena were observed and high frequency current was measured in the factory. We made experiments exposing a reel of yarn, television, and so on, to microwave. The results correspond to the phenomena observed in the factory.

articleTitle: Short Term Earthquake Prediction in Greece by Detecting Seismic Electric Signals
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since 1982 continuous monitoring of the earth's electric field is carried out at various sites of Greece. These sites have been carefully selected to be sensitive for the collection of Seismic Electric Signals (SES) which are transient changes of the electrotelluric field that precede earthquakes. Each of these sites is found to be sensitive only to certain seismic areas (selectivity effect). The physical properties of the SESs are briefly reviewed. Public warnings were issued after a proper analysis of the SES data and well before the two most destructive seismic activities. Furthermore a new type of an electromagnetic precursor is presented for the first time.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency E-Field Standard
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The work discusses methods applied to E-field meters standardization till now. Apart from low-frequency E-field measurements in far-field with loop antennas, in the nearfield, whip or dipole antennas are in use. The latter were standardized with the use of a TEM-cell or, on an open site, with the use of another whip antenna. For this purpose is proposed a similar standard as previously used for loop antennas standardization. It is more effective, less susceptible to interference and surroundings, easier in use and is more universal. A set of standard loop antenna was designed and comparative measurements of a short, symmetrical dipole antenna were performed. Results of measurements in a TEM-cell and with the use of the standard are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Measurement of Transfer Impedance above 500 Mhz by Using the Reverberating Chamber Method
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the measurement of shielding effectiveness with a method using a mode-stirred reverberating chamber. This method uses the characteristics of large oversized electromagnetic cavities. The advantage is that the radiation of the objects placed inside such a chamber appears isotropic. We can, by this way, estimate the shielding effectiveness with a very satisfactory reproductibility over a frequency range extending from 500 MHz up to few GHz. Three aspects will be described in this paper: the measurement of shielding effectiveness of connectors and cables. In this case, we present a method to convert this parameter to a transfer impedance. Finally, we will suggest an electromagnetic susceptibility test realized on an active electronic component.

articleTitle: Generation of Electromagnetic Interference in a Converter-Type Transmission System with a Direct Current-Motor
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents the results of research carried out on the electromagnetic interference generated in a power transmission system consisting of controlled rectifier and direct-current motor. The sources of interference appearing in the system have been determined and analysed. An interference damping circuit has been proposed, using an inductance-capacitance filter. Conclusions sum up the presentation.

articleTitle: Antenna Analysis and Optimization by Using the Probability Gain Criteria
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The antenna analysis and optimization on a view of EMC is presented. For scanning antennas and antennas, installed at mobile using facilities, new probability antenna characteristics, are proposed. The ways of their determination and calculation are outlined. The antenna aperture optimization problem, based on introduced criteria using, is formulated. Calculation aspects are discussed and optimization methods are worked out. For antenna arrays some illustration examples are presented.

articleTitle: Influence of Utilization Conditions Communication Systems on the Problem of Electromagntic Compatibility
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper is devoted to a new study of the frequency/distance standards providing compatibility of communication systems. Adaptive standards are presented, based on the analysis of interaction of communication systems and calculation of useful signal and interference levels.

articleTitle: Linearization of Electromagnetic Compatibility Models by Parametric Identification
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) models linearization by parametric identification, using Laplace's transformation and unit pulse responses of power consumers, permits to present them by simple model in appearance of a combination of some elementary links. The procedure of the linear modeling with use of this approach as well as its application for an EMC estimation are displayed. The application of presented method in detail is illustrated by the simulation of active and reactive powers alteration dynamics of synchronous motors when terminal voltage changes.

articleTitle: Computation of Common Mode Radiation Due to Asymmetric Coupling on Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Common mode radiation often is the predominant contribution to the overall radiation from printed circuit boards. Since the return paths for common-mode currents are via displacement current, the proximity of the printed transmission lines to nearby metal objects become important. It is shown that common mode currents are due to the asymmetry of the printed structures, and therefore, an effective reduction of the overall radiation will be obtained by designing symmetrically printed circuits.

articleTitle: Design of Remotely Computer-Controlled Integrated Spectrum Observation Centres
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Canadian administration is developing an Integrated Spectrum Observation Centre (ISOC) system of computer-controlled stations located at remote sites to monitor the radio frequency spectrum from 10 KHz to 1800 MHz. This system has a star network configuration allowing a central site to control a number of unattended remote monitoring sites. The computer architecture is based on the OS/2 operating system using LAN/WAN networks and permits multi-user and multisite control of the remote instrumentation. The ISOC system is used for real-time spectrum analysis and technical parameter measurement in support of Canadian spectrum management. This network will be integrated with a distributed data base to provide efficient processing of collected data to meet both operational and planning needs.

articleTitle: Simple Analitical, Method for Calculation of Voltage in Aeriel Lines from Transient Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a symple analytical method for calculation of total voltage due to transient electromagnetic fields in semi-infinitely aeriel line over a plane ground surface. The influence of horizontal and vertical field components and finite ground conductivity are taken into account. The method presented permits to evaluate the responses of an aeriel line with variable orientation and of different wave polarization. The calculation time is small and the errors are negligible.

articleTitle: Simulation Investigations of Overvoltages Caused by Lightning in Multiconductor Telecommunication Cables
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the usual procedure for predicting the expected lightning overvoltages in multiconductor telecommunication cables. By means of computer model an attempt was made to estimate the surge currents caused by lightning in the shields of telecommunication cables or in conducting elements that are close to cables. Next the laboratory measurements of longitudinal and transverse voltage surges in cables have been carried out. These surges were caused by currents which amplitudes and shapes were obtained from calculations.

articleTitle: The Effect of RF Discharge on the Operation of Vibrator Antennas
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We have investigated experimentally and theoretically the effect of RF discharge excited in a rare gus by the antenna field on the input and radiate on characteristics of the antenna. We have shown that the formation of plasma inhomogeneity can lead to increasing radiation power and to modification of antenna pattern, this process may be controlling.

articleTitle: Directional Patterns of UHF-Antennas Under Signal Reception Beyond the Horizon
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are given the experimental results of antenna pattern distortions investigation for beyond-the-horizon UHF propagation over the sea path up to 500km long. There are measured the statistical parameters, which can be used for estimation of the interferences from beyond-the-horizon scanning sources of powerful microwave radiation. A statistical model for the attenuation factor depending on angle orientation of radiating directional antenna for beyond-the-horizon propagation is proposed.

articleTitle: Coordination of Satellite Earth Station with Aeronautical Services and Airborne Equipment
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper, an example of analysis of possible localisation for satellite earth station (SES) designed for TV programs retransmission from Poland to the United States is presented. The possibility of co-existence the earth satellite station and communication airport is examined. A method of analysis an interferences is described. An example of results are shown.

articleTitle: Education in EMC at Technical University Brno
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The contribution deals with the concept of graduate EMC education at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science TU Brno in the Czech Republic. At the last year, the grant project supported by the Ministry of Education Czech Republic was solved at the Institute of Radioelectronics TU Brno. The principle aims of the project are presented in the contribution and contents of various courses with included EMC aspects. Also the syllabus of a special dedicated course "Electromagnetic Compatibility" is given here.

articleTitle: Multifactorial Tests for Noise Immunity of Microelectronic Systems Ensuring Railway Traffic Safety
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper shows the techniques of performing multifactorial tests for noise immuni ty using the methods of the mathematical experiment designing theory. This methodology allows to reveal the most significant factors of interfering noise and to evaluate their effect upon the noise immunity of a system. Application of the methods of the experiment designing theory in multi factorial tests significantly saves times and means and allows to evaluate the performance of noise protectors.

articleTitle: ESD-Immunity Tests Evaluation of the Test Results from a Probabilistic Point of View
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: From practical experience it is known that accuracy and reproducibility of the test results, obtained from standardized ESD-test procedures are unsatisfying in many cases. Assuming the ESD-immunity factor being a random variable that phenomenon can be explained and quantified. Related problems will be discussed in the present paper.

articleTitle: Observed Direct Lightning Current Distribution at a Mountain-Top Radio Relay Station
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It has become very important to study the lightning surges that flows into telecommunications equipment because of the increased use of susceptible circuit to over voltages. This paper reports for the first time the simultaneous measurements of the distributed lightning current at many positions in a mountain-top radio relay station caused by natural direct lightning strikes. More than 90% of the direct lightning current flows into the antenna tower legs and waveguides, with the high frequency components of the lightning current tending to flow into the outside parts of those structural components. Using these results, lightning current occurrence probabilities at the waveguide and cables were estimated by analyzing the transfer factors between current waveforms at those components.

articleTitle: Polarization Pure, Low Sidelobe Radiator for 1-4 GHz Radio Links Application
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The suitability of surface-wave radiating structures for generating of low crosspolarization, low sidelobe axially symmetrical beam is considered. It is concluded that disk-on- rod radiating structure when used in 1-4 GHz frequency band can provide a significant performance advantage over commonly used antenna types. Parametric optimization technique involving accurate analysis procedure on each step was used for synthesis of antenna geometry. Design example of compact 20-dB gain, low sidelobe, polarization pure antenna for 2-GHz frequency band is presented.

articleTitle: On the Crosstalk Reduction in Printed-Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of crosstalk in printed-circuit boards is investigated. The possibility of simplificated prediction of crosstalk values is substantiated. Ways of an electromagnetic coupling reduction in printed-circuit boards are discussed. Characteristics of coupled suspended microstrip lines and coupled inverted miorostrip lines with various parameters of substrate and isolating layer between the substrate and the ground plane are calculated by variational method. It is shown, that by means of proper choice of the dielectrics parameters the crosstalk values in printed-circuit boards with such lines may be reduced considerably.

articleTitle: Cochannel Interference in Instrument Landing Systems
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This work reports on cochannel interferences originating from sources in the coverage area of the localizer beam of an instrument landing system. The interfering sources can produce a valid false runway axis in space which may deviate an aircraft in automatic flight conditions from the prescribed approach route. Such sources may originate from ISM equipment.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Investigation of Electromagnetic Fields Generated by Rail Guns
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic launch systems such as rail guns generate electromagnetic signatures that contain a spectrum of frequencies extending from quasi-DC up to tens of kHz. EMC considerations pertaining to the potential adverse effects of these fields on nearby electronic equipment remain, however, largely unexplored. This paper addresses theoretical models used to predict the transient behavior of the currents produced in the rail gun structure, the dynamical generation of the external fields, experimental techniques used to measure the fields, and a comparison of theoretical models with experimental data.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of Lightning Induced Voltage on High Voltage Overhead Line Using a New Method for Lightning Channel Effects
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a new analytical method is presented for lightning induced voltage and current in 33 kV overhead line. Lightning channel is modelled by monopole antenna. The excitation generator of proposed antenna is such that the current distribution of channel with respect to time and space is based on TL (transmision Une) model Due to transient wave form of electromagnetic field caused by lightning and also due to rapid change of current in TL model with respect to time, the Maxwell's equations in time domain have been used. For this purpose the solution of electric field integral equation (EFIE), solved by the method of moment (MOM), in time domain, provides electromagnetic field caused by lightning stroke at any point, and any time. It is clear that with above method, the coupling effect between lightning channel and 33 kV overhead Une can be analysed conveniently. Thus the time variation of induced current and voltage at any point of line can be obtained. Therefore the protective scheme for 33 kV line can be selected accurately.

articleTitle: International Standardization in the Field of Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper has two main aims: - to describe the organization and the structure of the standardization work on electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) at the world level. - to explain, in the context of the general cooperation agreement between the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardization (CENELEC), the contribution of the IEC to the implementation of the EMC Directive of the European Union (EU).

articleTitle: On the Thunderstorm Overvoltages in 3-Wire Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A mathematical model of the thunderstorm overvoltages in 3-wire transmission lines caused by a lightning which can be used in the permafrost zone is suggested. The notion of a nondistorting 3-wire transmission line is introduced. A system of nine algebraic relations between distributed parameters of such line generalizing the known "undistorted signal transmission" condition is found. It is shown that the main cause of an overvoltages in the nondistorting 3- wire line induced by the lightning discharge is a current and voltage wave appearance due to spreading of charges pulled by the thundercloud electrostatic field.

articleTitle: Cispr Immunity Requirements and Intermodulation EV FM Receivers
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Non-linear phenomenon in the FM receivers input stages and its implications on the interference in radio reception are discussed. CISPR Publication 20 requirements for internal immunity are mainly connected with crossmodulation. It is proved on base of the broad practical investigations and on some theoretical dependencies. So, the problem of the FM receiver immunity against intermodulation is still opened. Authors define appropriate parameter that is a good measure of FM receiver's intermodulation immunity. Its value may be easily established on the base of very simple measurements. At the same time it allows to predict the receiver's behaviour indifferent situations.

articleTitle: On the Electromagnetic Compatibility of Selected Spread Spectrum Systems
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work we consider two applications of Spread Spectrum (SS) techniques. The first of which is the application of Direct Sequence (DS) SS to RF channels and the second to a lesser known application of SS, namely Local Power Grid (LPG) communications. To the former the method of maximum entropy is used to accurately estimate the probability density function of the interuser interference of a Spread Spectrum Multiple Access (SSMA) system. From this the EM interference to narrowband users is estimated and a standard for the number of overlaid SS users is recommended. In the case of LPG communications, which is a viable solution to communications in third world countries, we categorise the different types of noise encountered in this very hostile environment experimentally. Under these conditions we adopt a different approach and suggest slightly more stringent EMI/EMC standard requirements for household electrical appliances to make such a scheme technically viable.

articleTitle: Development on ISN and CDN for EMC Measurement at Telecommunication Ports
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The widespread application of digital LSIs and microprocessors technologies to telecommunications equipment has resulted in a large increase in electromagnetic interference as well as a deterioration in noise-immunity. This has created a need to develop the measurement methods of disturbance and immunity at telecommunication ports. CISPR and IEC have been discussing the measurement methods. An impedance stabilization network (ISN) and a coupling and decoupling network (CDN) have been developed for the measurement of disturbance and immunity. This paper presents the ISN and CDN which are recently developed in Japan and shows that the ISN and CDN meet the requirements proposed by CISPR and IEC.

articleTitle: Effect of Interaction Between Large- and Small-Scale Disturbances on Stability of Atmospheric Flows
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: More applicable model for description of dynamics of turbulence in stratified shear flows is used to improve analysis of interaction between large-scale waves and small-scale turbulence in atmospheric stratified shear flows, which was reported by authors together with V.A. Buts and P.I. Kolykhalov at 1990 Wroclaw EMC Symposium [1] as an example of new approach to studies of influence of fluctuations and external noise on dynamics of continuous systems.

articleTitle: EM Compatibility Among Multiple LEO and MEO MSS Satellite Networks using CDMA
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mobile Satellite Services (MSSs) represent one of the fastest growing segment of the satellite industry. Besides the existing satellite networks in geostationary satellite orbit (GSO), that currently provide voice and data communications for a variety of land-, maritime- and aeronautical-based applications, new mobile satellite sendees are just around the comer. These new systems, employing multiple satellite constellations in low and medium earth orbits (LEOs, MEOs), are aiming to deliver a whole new level of service, i.e. a world-wide communications via handheld telephones. In a communications scenario where the spectrum utilization is at present already a problem within certain regions, the entrants of these systems will make the spectral congestion a very serious problem on a world-wide basis. Since non-geostationary satellites will pass over all countries in their orbits around the world, a global coordination will be required for these systems. This will make the future satellite communications scenario much more crowded and, because of the spectral resources even more congestioned, much more complicated to be coordinated. Thus, in order to enhance spectrum efficiency, new methodologies and techniques, including design choices and operating parameters, need to be identified and developed, thus permitting independent satellite systems to share the same bands. Systems employing spread spectrum techniques (CDMA) may be one way to improve the efficiency of spectrum utilization. The aim of this paper is to explore the nature of the interference between different satellite communications networks. In particular, preliminary considerations are made upon interference aspects relating multiple CDMA satellite communications network operating co-coverage and cofrequency in LEOs and/or MEOs. The interference mechanism that affects the forward link from the gateway earth station (GES) to the LEO/MEO satellite to the mobile earth station (MES) is described in the case of interference on the down-link at the MES, from other networks' satellites simultaneously sharing the same frequency within the same service area. To evaluate the interference impact on the forward link (down-link), the total power flux density (PFSD) is introduced for each system. Then, the effect of one system on another is calculated in terms of the system capacity reduction. From the coordination process viewpoint, it is introduced the concept of maximum permissible PFSDs established by the International Organizations, and the maximum desirable PFSDs that are being specified at any point of the service area by each satellite system (Administration) involved in the coordination process. Then, a criterion is proposed for establishing whether or not coordination among CDMA satellite networks is required. With regard to this, it is also shown that if coordination is required, this could be solved through a reduction in capacity, not necessarily implying the loss of all the capacity associated with the spread bandwidth.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of Electromagnetic Radiation Spectrum of Power Klystrons
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Klystrons are widely used as power amplifiers in various radio engineering systems. That is why the simulation of their electromagnetic radiation spectrum is an actual problem. It can be solved ohly within rigorous non-linear theory taking into account multi-freguency character of signals, non-linear processes in electron beam and resonator properties. In the paper non-linear multi-freguency theory or klystron based on new results of electrodynamic systems excitation and on wave description of electron beam is developed. It allows to simulate electromagnetic radiation spectrum of klystron with high accuracy. On the base of the theory the program for computer IBM PC 386/387 has been created that allows to solve a wide range of problems connected with spectrum analysis and sygnal distortion.

articleTitle: Low Frequency and Medium Frequency Radiowave Propagation Along a Permafrost Paths
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Results of the experimental investigation low and medium frequency radiowaves propagation above a permafrost paths are presented. Radiowave attenuation in different seasons of year are considered and the experimental results were compared with the theory of ground wave propagation.

articleTitle: Spectrum Occupancy Indicator in Case of Frequency Sharing Between Adaptive and Non-Adaptive Stations
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new spectrum occupancy indicator is suggested. It allows to estimate the possibility of frequency bands sharing between adaptive and non-adaptive stations. A technique of its calculation is also suggested.

articleTitle: Study of Electromagnetic Interference Generated by Various Sources on Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electric discharges on transmission lines can be sources of electromagnetic interference (EMI). Radio interference from corona discharges on conductor can be limited by the adequat choice of a conductor diameter, the number of subconductor per phase and subconductor spacing. EMI from transmission line can be also generated by local sources of corona discharges on protruding parts of line fittings, as well as other types of electric discharges (discharges in fittings gaps, creeping discharges on insulators). Electric discharges peculiarities were studied on the basis of oscillograms. Use of interference oscillograms from transmission lines with application of special methods and devices permits to locate interference, to determine courses of its appearance and to find means of its elimination.

articleTitle: Decreasing Levels of Lateral and Back Radiations of Vibrator and Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Using the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction there has been solved three-dimensional problem of radiating vibrator with an ideally conducting rectangular plane screen and microstrip antennas.
