For a detailed quantitative analyses of a spacial radiation- structure of the investigated systems and effects of sizes and forms of a screen there were worked out algorithms and programs of calculating normalized amplitude directive patterns in different observation planes. Analysis of the calculated Front to Back Ratios, when changing sizes of the screen over wide ranges, has proved possibility of sufficient decreasing levels of the back and lateral radiation by means of choosing an appropriate ratio of screen sides.

articleTitle: A Review of Current High Power Microwave Sources
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A review of high power microwave sources (HPM) includes relativistic magnetrons, magnetically insulated transmission line oscillators (MILOSs), gyrotrons, vircators, intense relativistic electron beam devices, backward traveling wave oscillators, and "Chirp" pulse compression radars. Analytical and experimental results are presented for coaxial MILOs. Unique aspects of MILO designs are Chebyshev transformer sections which match slow wave source structures to fast wave output structures. "Chirp" pulse compression is also presented for HPM applications in both transmit and receive modes.

articleTitle: Scattering Parameter Transient Analysis of Field Coupling to Lossy MTLs
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we extend the transient scattering analysis of a lossy multiconductor transmission line (MTL) to the evaluation of the interference produced by a field illuminating the line. The proposed formulation fully exploits the advantages of the transient analysis based on the line matched scattering parameters, dealing effectively with low-loss lines and helping the understanding of the interference mechanism through the physical interpretation of the results.

articleTitle: Analysis of RFI Measured by C.I.S.P.R. Test Receiver
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is considered a method calculating radio interferences coming to the test receiver input which meets the C.I.S.P.R. requirments for radio interference measuring apparatus. The quasi-peak measurement algorithm is based on the analysis of a signal pass through the channel consisting of a narrow band-pass filter, a quasi-peak detector and an indicating instrument. The peculiarity of the method is in the definition of the envelope on the narrow band-pass filter output under which found value is also calculated the peak, average and r.m.s. voltages of the interferences. It is given examples of the radio interferences calculation results by detectors different types.

articleTitle: A New Method of Direction Finding for VLF Radio Waves with Any Wave Polarisations
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We discuss a method for estimating wave distribution function (WDF) independently of wave polarisation, which is an important technique to discuss the propagation and generation mechanisms of VLF radio waves, including magnetospheric VLF waves, tweek atmospherics, waves from transmitter and so on. A new treatment to estimate WDF solution of VLF waves observed on the ground is discussed. This is very effective method to discuss the propagation and generation mechanisms of VLF radio waves, because it is possible to estimate the WDF, or wave energy distribution in wave number space. It is confirmed, by computer simulation, that this method is effective to discuss the propagation characteristics of VLF waves, and also it is found from analysis of VLF emissions that the ionospheric exit region moves very fast.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Field Inside Anechoic Chamber of Rectangular Shape
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An anechoic chamber is essentially characterized by the assured low level of reflections. However, for the most part, currently available chambers provide such a level only in that part of their inner space which is called the uniformity (or anechoic) region. Geometry (form, size) of the uniformity region is known as essentially depending on: • geometry of the anechoic chamber itself • absorbing material • radiating region (sours region in chamber) • operating frequency.

articleTitle: EMC Issues of Wide PCB Buses
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A device under test with 17 coupled microstrip traces was constructed, built, and measured. It is shown that the near-end time-domain crosstalk waveform has a peak around the trailing edge, and the region of traces over which crosstalk must be considered spans over several adjacent traces.

articleTitle: Wrocław Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes the first testing site in Poland located in an anechoic chamber - the first such civilian site, at any rate. The site enables antenna, emission and susceptibility testing to be conducted. The site simulates both "free space" and "open field" conditions. The chamber's parameters and area of application are discussed below.

articleTitle: Research of the Lightning Electromagnetic Fields Structure for Tests Radioelectronic Equipment on the Conformity with Requirement of Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper investigates the structure of electromagnetic fields radiated by the negative lightning "cloud-earth" for near and far zone. The majority of the natural factors that produce a certain influence on the lightning shaping have been taken into account. These factors are the nonuniform velocity of the return stroke, the shape of the current flowing in the lightning channel and its amplitude and time characteristics, path tortuosity of the channel, lenght of the channel, the finite conduction of the ground, the interaction processes between the electromagnetic lightning radiation and the ground surface and the spreading of the lightning current in the ground. The new representation of the electromagnetic fields in the nearzone radiation of lightning has been suggested. According to it, the electromagnetic fields are represented by the rapidly changing component lightning electromagnetic pulse (LEMP) and electric (LEP) and magnetic (LMP) field pulses slowly changing in time, it is shown that this representation is convenient for the simulation of electromagnetic fields produced by the lightning. The simulation of electromagnetic fields is required for the electromagnetic compatibility tests of radioelectronic equipment (REE) influenced the lightning.

articleTitle: Observation of Large-Scale Irregularity of the Lower Ionosphere, Based on the Propagation Characteristics of Tweek Atmospherics
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We will discuss a new technique to observe the ionospheric height with satisfactory accuracy, based on the propagation characteristics of tweek atmospherics (small dispersion effect in the Earth-ionosphere waveguide). It is shown that the dispersion of the Earth-ionosphere waveguide is determined by the propagation distance and effective reflection height in the lower ionosphere, even when taking account of the Earth's magnetic field in the ionosphere, and how to analyze non-stationary signal such as atmospherics. And we introduce an interesting phenomenon of the lower ionosphere related to K<inf>p</inf> index.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility in Power Engineering: Frequency Characteristics - Measurements and Calculations
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Harmonic currents propagation from nonlinear - sources is influenced substantially in electrical networks by their frequency characteristics. Measurement and calculation procedures have been worked out to determine these characteristics. The authors deal with both the procedures in this paper and present a methodology of frequency characteristics measurements in brief. At the same time, they discuss possibilities of calculation in more complicated networks by means of a dominant transformer consumption method.

articleTitle: Amplifier with Linear Feedback for 2nd- and 3rd- Order Intermodulation Products
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Using a special type of linear negative feedback we present an efficient technique for compensation of nonlinearities in amplifiers. It is shown that the presented technique achieves a considerably higher performance than conventional negative linear feedback. The 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd- order Volterra transfer functions of the amplifier, the condition to introduce feedback only for intermodulation products and the deep of diminishing nonlinearities were obtained. In order to obtain these results the Volterra series representation and the structural theory of systems were combined.

articleTitle: Power Lines Interference: Effective Suppression at Low Frequencies
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some important problems of power lines interference suppression are beine considered in the report. The original devices to solve effectively the problem of power lines interferences suppression at low frequencies are suggested. Experimental results has confirmed high efficiency of these devices.

articleTitle: Ropes of a Winding Machine as a Line for Shaft Communication System
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transport of personnel and material in shafts as well as inspection of shafts requires a reliable, easy to use shaft communication system, that transfers a signal between the winding house and cages in shafts. Many shaft communication systems use the hoisting ropes as a transmission line. These systems operate in the long wave frequency band. The paper presents an analysis of currents in ropes caused by transmitters in winding house station and cage station.. For shafts with two winding machines the paper presents an analysis of crosstalk between two shaft communication systems in the shaft. High power thyristor converters (for example rectifiers) are used for electric drive of winding machines. These converters are a source of electromagnetic interference for shaft communication systems. The paper presents results of measurements of the interference current in winding machine ropes.

articleTitle: A Comparative Numerical Study of Several Techniques for Predicting the Response of Two-Wire Transmission Line to Nonuniform Electromagnetic Field of a Nearby Source
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of a comparative study of a ’rigorous’ numerical approach employing the integral equation formulation and the method of moments, and transmission-line-theory approach to the problem of two-wire transmission line excited by a source (in the form of the linear antenna) in close proximity to the line are reported in the paper. The main goal of the study is to determine the limits of applicability of approximate transmission-line-theory approach to the problems in which strong electromagnetic interaction effects between source and victim circuit exist.

articleTitle: Reduction of Interference in Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio astronomical observations are increasingly affected by man-made interference of various kinds. Sophisticated software tools have to be developed to cope with interference effects in the data. These tools can be divided into two categories: [1] destructive for radio astronomical information; and [2] non-destructive for radio astronomical information. An example of [1] is rejection of data lying outside some deviation from a median for an interval running through the data cube. Examples of [2] are: (i) a ”frequency domain filtering" technique, which separates the astronomical information from the noisy background and interference effects; and (ii) prediction and subtraction of a narrowband carrier and its sidebands taking into account the frequency behaviour of the signal amplitude. The merits of the methods are discussed for different kinds of observations: i.e. single dish and interferometry, narrow and wide band observations.

articleTitle: Observation Results of Electromagnetic Field Intensity Distribution to Exposure of the Walkie-Talkie and Automobile and Biological Effects in Ham Radio
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper shows the measurement results of radiation electric field intensity distributions close to low power walkie-talkie equipments, and around and inside electric fields of automobile by means of 10 watt standard transmitter which they are used in Amature Radio Servise, on 2 meter, 70 cm and 24 cm amature bands.

articleTitle: Some Problems of Optimization of HF Broadcasting Links
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this article problems of reliability and optimum length of HF broadcasting links are discussed. The reliability is determined by change of relation signal/interference (S/I) from day to day for required hour within a month. The efficiency of diversity depends on many factors including degree of S/I correlation. The optimum length of broadcasting is determined with point of view of rational frequency use and decreeing of interference area.

articleTitle: Field Simulation of Lightning Electromagnetic Threats
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Problems of the field simulation of lightning electromagnetic threats in testing the vulnerability of electronic devices have been discussed. Attention has been given to the present data concerning the parameters of lightning discharge currents and the electromagnetic fields being generated as well as to particular significance of the magnetic component of the electromagnetic field as a source of interference. A new method has been proposed for testing electronic devices in the EMP simulator by means of chopped pulses which makes it possible to obtain a high magnetic component of EMP field. This method is relatively simple and offers possibilities of changing in the wide limits the peak value of the magnetic field intensity.

articleTitle: EMI Caused by ARS and Other Household Wireless Devices
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The present work examines selected EMI problems created by the Amateur Radio Service (ARS) and other services located within or near inhabited areas. The experiences of ARS provide good opportunities to study present EMI problems before new ones will be created by more and more radiation sources installed within households and nearby areas. Results of estimations of EMF levels in the vicinity of different antenna types are presented. They show that greater power may be radiated if its beam is well focused. Briefly discussed are voltages induced by a transmitting antenna in receiving ones as well as the role of resonant effects in household devices. In the appendix is shown an operators' hand- and lip-currents while using portable transmitters.

articleTitle: Radio Climate of the Coastal Region of Poland
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The atmosphere substantially affect the propagation of radio waves used in many communication systems, broadcast, radars etc.. Properties of the atmosphere, as well as phenomena in that layer which influence the radio wave propagation, depend on the climatic region. Therefore, one can still notice continous interest in investigations of regional radio wave propagation conditions. In the presented paper problems connected with the radio climate of the North of Poland are discussed.

articleTitle: PCB Emission Analysis in Different Image Planes Configurations
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An investigation has been performed to outline the main aspects regarding the radiated electromagnetic field which have to be accounted of in the PCB design. The influence of the image planes geometry on the radiation has been analyzed and it is shown how an optimal of the image plane dimensions can reduce the radiated field of some dB. The analysis has been conducted by applying the Method of Moments and taking into account the finite conductivity of the image planes.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of Planar Wire-Mesh Shields Loaded by Carbon Fibre Composite Slabs
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The analysis of the behaviour of a planar wire-mesh shield loaded by Carbon Fibre Composite slabs excited by an ElectroMagnetic Pulse - a NEMP - is here presented. The slabs are characterized in terms of trasmission matrices that lead to evaluate easily the shielded fields. A suitable model of the grating has been introduced in order to consider the occuring phenomena, in fact through a spectral technique the electromagnetic problem is translated into the equivalent circuit network model that allows to express the time response of the shielded field in a closed form.

articleTitle: Anti-Interference Measures at Nançay Radioastronomy Observatory
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The authors will describe a large set of measures taken at Nançay Radioastronomy Observatory against unwanted radio-emissions of different kinds in order to preserve the quality of the most sensitive radioastronomy observations. Among the steps already in process: - actions toward the frequency managers on national and international levels to sensibilize them to the specificity of Radioastronomy and the problems involved by passive observations of very weak sources. - struggle to preserving a very important band for OH line observations as well as future uses of the band around 1612 MHz against the GLONASS satellite navigation system, according to the primary status allocated by WARC-92. - construction and results of a sophisticated interference monitoring antenna and receiving system in the band 1-3 GHz. - study of the efficiency of a high (40 metres) shielding wall surrounding the Large Decimetric Radiotelescope. - research efforts on new techniques for excising manmade radio-interferences in real time data processing. - reducing the Nançay Radiotelescope susceptibility to interference by up-grading the feed system for a better antenna illumination.

articleTitle: Frequency Sharing Between Fixed and Radiolocation Services in HF Band
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A criterion of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) between adaptive radiolocation system (ARLS) and Fixed Service (FS) stations is suggested. A technique of EMC indicator calculating is also suggested. They may be used in EMC analysis during preparation stage of the frequency notification procedure for the ARLS in HF band and for determination the needs of coordination. Additionally, an algorithm of structure optimisation of the ARLS signal is suggested. This algorithm provides obtaining of larger signal-to-interference ratios for FS stations.

articleTitle: The Dependence of Antistress Effect of Millimeter Waves of Nonthermal Intensity on the Localization of the Influence in Rats with Various Typological Features
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic fields (EMF) of extremely High Frequency (EHF) find more and more use in medicine for a treating many diseases (Poslavsky et al., 1989, Golovacheva et al., 1989, Ronkin et al., 1991). We've accumulated experimental and clinical data, showing that the localization of the influence plays an important role in the increase of EHF-the- rapy effectiveness. That's why the pur pose of our investigation was the observation for the rats' reaction on the different localization of the EMF EHF in fluence.

articleTitle: Modeling of Electromagnetic Field Density Distribution in the Near-Earth Space
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a mathematical model of the terrestrial electromagnetic field that enables one to calculate spatio-temporal distributions of the electromagnetic field over the space about the Earth under different heliophysical conditions. The proposed model has been used in numerical experiments that assumed the broadcasting short wave radio stations to be the ground based sources of radio waves. The results of these numerical experiments are in a good agreement with data of ground based and spaceborne measurements of the electromagnetic field strength.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic Properties of Some Types of Layered and Gradient Conducting and Semiconducting Media
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Free space electromagnetic concordance with material media plays an important role in the problem of EMC. With the help of interfacing media numerous tasks of creating electromagnetic absorbers are being solved, this is of importantes for making anechoic chambers, radiotransparent covers and for solving many other problems. In view mathematics and calculation narrow band frequency electromagnetic energy absorbers are synthesized simply enough. Much more difficulties appear in synthesis of wide range absorbing layered media. To obtain rather small coefficient of reflection through the whole frequency band under consideration one has to increase the number of layers of the system and this, naturally complicates the solution of the problem EMC. The report is devoted to some new approaches to the solutions of these tasks on the basis of media, where analytical solutins. In the report based on the wave equation for E and H-polarized waves the analytical solutions for material, gradient media, in which change with the depth acceding to the defenite low have been considered. The generalization of Rayleigh's solution given for dielectric media, in case of conducting and semiconducting media is shown. Analytical expressions describing media are given too. Generalization of Rayleigh's solution in case of three-layered conducting and semiconducting media is made. Analytical expressions discribing impedance and reflecting characteristics of some types of gradient media have been also obtained. A class of dispersionless media concorded with free space (vacuume) has been revealed analytically. The model of such media can be expressed by the dependence of the type, where k, a - are some parameters of the model and z is a coordinate of axis z. The examples of dispersionless, semiconducting media with constant component of modul of the electric field are considered. It is also shown that the impedance of such media is real and doesn't depend on frequency. Analogous conclusion on considered electromagnetic properties of media has been drawn using Riccati’s equation. The relation between and has been found with the help of which such media are obtaind.

articleTitle: Placement on Printed Circuit Boards Under EMC and Thermic Constraints
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Due to new technologies and regulations, Electro-Magnetic Compatibility gets more and more importance for PCB-design [J-90]. Up to now, the commercial design systems contain simulation tools to find electromagnetic disturbances, but their automatic placement tools don't take it into consideration. In this paper we describe how to incorporate EMC and thermic rules into the PCB layout procedure.

articleTitle: Frequency Sharing Between Fixed and Radiolocation Services in HF Band
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A criterion of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) between adaptive radiolocation system (ARLS) and Fixed Service (FS) stations is suggested. A technique of EMC indicator calculating is also suggested. They may be used in EMC analysis during preparation stage of the frequency notification procedure for the ARLS in HF band and for determination the needs of coordination. Additionally, an algorithm of structure optimisation of the ARLS signal is suggested. This algorithm provides obtaining of larger signal-to-interference ratios for FS stations.

articleTitle: Study of Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Effect on Multiconductor Wires
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The description of wave processes used the theory of long wires is well known. Long wires are usually assumed to be multi-linked chained equivalent circuits. In this paper both wave nature of process in the wire and the actual frequency response of a system element was suggested. The efficient method of solution of the transient process in the multiconductor wires under the EMP effect was proposed also. The numerous calculation examples for self-contained underground power supplies, electromechanical apparatus, control relay elements were made.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional TLM Model of a Tem Cell
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Institute of Telecommunications and Acoustics (ITA) Crawford TEM cell has been numerically modelled using three-dimensional Transmission-Line Matrix (TLM) method. Resonant frequencies as well as field distribution at different frequencies have been successfully calculated. The results have been compared with values measured using HP 8752A Network Analyzer and with results of calculations using other methods. The empty cell has been investigated as well as the cell with the metal object inside it.

articleTitle: Nowstationary Skin-Effect in the Wires of high Voltage Aerial Line and Damping of Nanosecond Current Pulse
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The technique of analytical calculation of wave processes in suspended above the ground nonmagnetic solid and tubular cylindric wires of two-wire homogeneous aerial line influenced by the nanosecond current pulse has been developed. It allows to determine the influence of nonstationary skin-effect and caused by it heat generation in circular wires of arbitrary thickness as well as geometrical and electrophysical parameters of aerial line for distortion and damping of the current running wave in nanosecond range. It is shown, that for current wave τ<sub>f</sub>/τ<sub>p</sub>=5/200 nanosec inducted in line by high altitude electromagnetic pulse (EMP) of nuclear explosion the pulse heat losses of energy in massive wires cause the considerable smoothing of wave front and damping of current wave amplitude. In case of nonmassive wires there is no deformation of pulse wave front due to joule losses of energy in wires metal, one can observe only its damping. It is established, that in nanosecond region intensity of wave processes damping in an aerial line increases with decrease in values of wires suspension above the ground, outer radius, wall thickness and conductivity of wires material. The obtained results can be used in both physics and technics of pulse processes in electromagnetic compatibility region and nanosecond pulse technics of modem physics experiment with energy high density which carry out at the electrophysical plants.

articleTitle: Considerations Followed in the Development of Longitudinal Inductions Test Methods
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the considerations followed by the Telecommunication Standardization Sector of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU-T, formerly CCITT) in development of longitudinal induction methods, used for simulating a two-wire line loop in a multi pair telecommunication cable exposed to power line induction. The distribution of the induced longitudinal emf is taken into consideration by the centre-of-exposure concept introduced by W.N.Bell. The equivalent common mode capacitances of a pair is identified for different common mode condition of the remaining pairs on the bases of measurements.

articleTitle: Design of Anechoic Chambers for Radiated EMC Testing by Computer Modelling
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A computer program is described which allows accurate prediction of the performance of anechoic chambers used for radiated EMC testing. The mathematical model is based on a ray-tracing technique taking into account multiple reflections. The absorber-lined surfaces are modelled by an equivalent complex reflection coefficient. For illustration, a comparison is made between the predicted and measured Normalised Site Attenuation for a 3m semi- anechoic chamber. Field Uniformity predictions are also given for the same chamber.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Effect of Septum Thickness on the Characteristic Impedance of a Symmetric Tem Cell
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a method for accounting the effect of septum thickness on the characteristic impedance of a symmetic TEM cell using the Schwarz-Christoffel transformation. The co-ordinates on the equipotential line which is coincident with the conducting septum boundaries are expressed as an explicit function of the variables appearing in the Schwarz-Christoffel transformation and are determined by solving a set of simultaneous non linear equations which are obtained by separating the incomplete elliptic integrals into real and imaginary parts. This method enables the estimation of characterisitic impedance as a function of thickness of the septum from a knowledge of change of capacitance due to the reduction of spacing between the parallel plates in the final transformed parallel plate configuration of TEM cell.

articleTitle: Assignment of Broadcast Frequencies by Utilizing Stochastic Optimization and Digital Terrain Database
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a method of assigning frequencies for local VHF-FM sound and TV broadcasting stations. The approach is based on the test point concept and stochastic optimization using simulated annealing algorithms. For propagation calculations an up to date digital terrain model (DTM) and data base is used. The aim of the work is to exploit the "topographic reserve" of the frequency resource in order to satisfy the rapidly growing demand for local program transmissions and to preserve the electromagnetic compatibility of the network. The novelty of the method is attributed to improvements of the optimization algorithm and to the selection of test points according to the capabilities of the DTM.

articleTitle: On the Programme of the EMC Symposium, Wroclaw 1994
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For the first time this year we have included three special sessions, in which an invited speakers give an extended review of important subject.

articleTitle: Radiated Susceptibility Test Limits for Motor Vehicles
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic environment (EME) of the motor vehicle is described. The present state of EMC standards for radiated susceptibility (RS) testing is presented. A classification of vehicle electronics with respect to its safety in case of malfunctions caused by EMI is proposed. A possible way of defining a 'representative' EMC for the motor vehicle is shown, so that EMC limits for RS testing can be established. Finally, examples of RS test limits applied in the automotive industry are presented.

articleTitle: The International Framework of Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The radio frequency spectrum is being used by a growing variety of radio services. The traditional uses of broadcasting, maritime and aeronautical communications, point to point fixed links, land mobile radio and numerous navigation services remain, but in almost every category new applications are being introduced at a growing pace and novel uses of radio spectrum are being exploited. Recent years have seen a dramatic change to digital modulation techniques, both in fixed and mobile services and the next generation of digital broadcasting services are close to implementation. There is increasing interest in the field of satellite communications to provide mobile services and more generally radio is providing the means to introduce quickly new telecommunication services, to provide competition in developed countries and to provide basic telephone services in developing countries. All of these applications have to co-exist alongside scientific and hobby use of radio and against a background of radio frequency emissions from nonradiocommunication sources.

articleTitle: Biological Effects of Electro Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The interpretation of the biological effects that can be observed in living tissues exposed to EMF requires a good quantitative description of the fields within the tissues. These one are a complex function of the frequency, the source configuration, the shape, the conformation, the size and the orientation in the field of the exposed subject. The maximum and average absorbed power density may vary over many orders of magnitude for the same applied field intensities. The energy distribution within the subject depends on multiple parameters that are analyzed. The biological effects of RF are complex and divided in two groups: - the thermal effects, including locally various physiopathologic reactions in the tissues and used by diathermy; one of them, the caractogenesis, appears if the power density is about 150 mW cm -the "specific" effects, where are reported: the effects on the Central Nervous System (alterations of EEG, sleep, changes in drug action), the behavioral effects, the effects on endocrine and immune systems observed in cell's culture as in mammals. From the results of these investigations, the characteristics of these bioeffects are reviewed. The biological effects of ELF are reviewed with special attention to the window effect. Since observations concerning effects of ELF on men are poor, epidemiological studies were done which are reported and discussed. Conclusions are given.

articleTitle: Patron's Address
publicationTitle: Twelfth International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This is for the twelfth time that such an eminent assembly of EMC experts meets together here in Wroclaw to present and exchange an information on most recent research achievements in this field. EMC becomes more and more important with respect to proper operating and co-existence of various telecommunications systems, to protection of telecommunications and electrical power supply systems against electrostatic or electromagnetic pulse discharge and also to protection of human beings against the harmful influence of electromagnetic fields in the large spectrum from extra low up to very high frequencies. I am very glad to have an opportunity to address these few words to the participants of this Symposium, not only as the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications, but also as a former, for more than twenty years, director of the Institute of Telecommunications in Warsaw. The Wroclaw branch of this Institute, together with the Technical University of Wroclaw, took the initiative to organize in this city the first EMC Symposium as early as in 1972. This made the Wrocław conference the oldest regular EMC Symposium in Europe. Together with its sister counterpart, the Zurich EMC Symposium, it became one of the most important EMC Symposia in Europe and one highly appreciated overseas as well.
